newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa urges Angola to keep to peace plan.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa urges Angola to keep to peace plan.

text.p: South Africa said on Tuesday Angola's peace timetable should not be delayed over the uncertain future of former rebel UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi in a unity government with the MPLA.

"We must not delay the Lusaka timetable any more. It is in the interests of everybody not to link the implementation of the Lusaka Protocol with the special status of Savimbi," deputy foreign minister Aziz Pahad told a parliamentary media briefing.
"It is in the interest of Angola for the UNITA deputies to return (to Luanda) and for a government of national unity to be established," Pahad said.

Savimbi, still refusing to leave his central highlands stronghold around Bailundo town, is insisting on talks with the government on his role in a new government and a programme for reconciliation ahead of the formation of a unity government.
The United Nations special envoy to Angola, Alioune Blondin Beye and foreign mediators held five-hour discussions with Savimbi at his headquarters on Monday.
But officials close to the peace process said the talks with Savimbi were strained.
"He still wants this dialogue with the government and he wants the special status sorted out," one official told Reuters.
The formation of a unity government is the next crucial step in Angola's two-year-old peace process to end 19 years of civil war between government and UNITA forces.
Both sides signed a peace pact in the Zambian capital Lusaka in 1994 to end the fighting.
Foreign governments are urging both sides to fulfill their peace agreements ahead of a gradual pullout of the 7,000-strong U.N. peacekeeping mission helping to implement Angola's peace plan.
